dimensions.note: Two recurring patterns are analyzed with rivals kept open. Effort and pleasure held together: concealed strain and comparison with specialists in two fields (B0199 H:P170-P183), a recovered first pleasure followed at once by a higher bar (H:P205-P231, P245), more than thirty minutes on one move beside 'I simply like moving' (B0248 505018301 EV-B0248-027, -029), an art interest she thinks unlike her (B0232 case 15) and a receiver's surprise at being celebrated (B0239 P11-P12). Care joined to unchecked inference: a partial observation becomes a protective model she never verifies and retains at the ending (B0255 EV-B0255-003, -006, -024, -044; CL-B0255-002). Not C: no conditional procedure for an unshown situation is derived, and B0255's mechanism is one family's comic premise. Not E: both patterns recur with rivals tested across independently gated readings.

Only B0199 H (strain, low bar, choice, higher bar, reported recovery) and B0255's six chapters (inference, protection, burden, disclosure, retained belief) have internal sequences. The readings refuse any order across the occurrences; 'pre-debut' (B0248), 'after the completed live' (B0251 200500) and summer (B0250, B0255) are local horizons, not a chronology. E rather than NOT_ASSESSED because the readings affirmatively establish that the occurrences are unordered.

Located written markers are few and mostly comic effects: the message title and manager address (B0232 case 15), くすぐったい for being surprised (B0239 P11-P12), and in B0255 her broken repetitions and wind-distorted spelling (chapter 1), publicly ambiguous ガードが甘い/心配 with private カツラの！！ (chapter 4), the cut-off ハげッごほんげっほん (chapter 5) and こないだ (chapter 2). Elsewhere her Japanese is paraphrased, no reading describes her ordinary register, and every voice cue is unheard. Not D: the located wording is too thin and too premise-bound to support voice.

Ordinary activities with stated reasons recur: running, shoe shopping and choosing a cute design (B0199 F, H2-H3), a solo museum visit (B0232), drinks for the trio and reluctant skin care (B0248 505018301, 505018304), doughnuts and tea during practice (B0250 EV-B0250-022, -023), a home-party plan and shopping invitation (B0251 508021701), and liking beach volleyball, warning about sea breeze and going out for air (B0255 EV-B0255-019, -020, -031). Many are proposed rather than shown. Not C: no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation. Not E: located across six readings.

Distinct, located conduct toward several counterparts: the manager (requests, protests at overprotection and touch, the requested back slap; B0199 H; unrequested protection and the final assurance and sea restriction, B0255 EV-B0255-006, -042, -043), Kyoko (reads her strictness as responsibility and prompts her concession, B0250 EV-B0250-013, -014; gives the requested shoulder while misreading the tears, B0255 EV-B0255-016), Honoka (teasing corrected and apologized for, B0248 EV-B0248-037, B0251 508021704; stops her contact and blocks her consultation, B0255 EV-B0255-024, -028), Sui (athletic rivalry and rematch, B0250), Coney (the audience-discovery idea, B0251 507020702) and the written board voices (B0239 P20-P22). Not C: no recipient rule is derived and most relations sit inside single families. Not E: the counterparts receive differentiated, located conduct.

B0255 supplies a sustained printed private-thought track across all six chapters: the secret she believes she saw, the resolve to cooperate, the head that prevents her concentration, the suspicion that Honoka will expose the truth, the wish she had never learned it and suffering since that day (EV-B0255-003, -006, -022, -027, -032), each analyzed against the reader's greater knowledge. Beside it are B0199 H's inward lines (P251-P252) and recalled first jump (P205-P216), B0239's receiver's surprise (P11-P12) and B0248's parenthesized no-comment appraisal (EV-B0248-042). Not C: the sustained track serves one false premise and supports no general model of her inner life. Not E: one family-length interior is analyzed chapter by chapter. A reviewer may prefer E.

B0255 analyzes her part in a family-long coordination conflict from cause to repair: protective interventions that suppress colleagues' concerns and block a consultation (CL-B0255-002, -016, -020), then joining the reflection, acknowledging the disclosure cost and proposing the simultaneous shout (EV-B0255-035 to -037; CL-B0255-028). Elsewhere friction is local and usually repaired: protests at being carried and grasped (B0199 H:P92-P95, P157-P160), the contested 'courting' exchange (H:P274-P275), the hook joke corrected and apologized for (B0248 EV-B0248-037), the leader-capacity prompt in the practice-slot dispute (B0250 EV-B0250-014) and the apology to Honoka (B0251 508021704). Not C: one analyzed process, inside a misunderstanding comedy, gives no conditional model. Not E: a conflict process is now analyzed across a whole family beside recurrent local repairs. A reviewer may prefer E.

Located normative content: apologies after teasing (B0248 EV-B0248-037; B0251 508021704), recognition of the staff labor behind idol work (B0251 508021701), a warning against jumping into the game (B0250 EV-B0250-019), and wanting to tell what she hid despite possible trouble for the manager (B0255 EV-B0255-037), which the reading calls a situated choice rather than a general mandate. None is deliberation through a dilemma. Not D: local acts only.

Teasing recurs and each reading tests it against its costs: the withdrawn pet joke and the water-sharing tease (B0199 E, H:P79), the framing and leggings jokes that draw peer objections (B0248 CL-B0248-047, -051), the planned teasing of the manager (CL-B0248-059), the proximity tease (B0250 CL-B0250-024), the teasing apology (B0251 508021704), Kyoko's board caution about teasing (B0239 P20-P22), and laughter about the relationship rumors after the well (B0255 EV-B0255-040). In B0255 she is mainly the comic object of her own misreading rather than a joker. Not C: no generative model. Not E: an analyzed recurring device across six readings.

Seven complete units: one Intimacy family including the 290-page episode, one Short message, one Birthday portfolio and five Event families in four readings. The main-story states the readings cite as context (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, which is the decisive gap for a main-cast character. Not D: narrow for the subject.

Affirmative limits recur: overwork named by the shopkeeper and by her own later account (B0199 H:P140-P146, P264), the complaint that she would dance forever (H:P266-P267), Honoka's and Kyoko's objections to body jokes (B0248 505018301, 505018303), the correction of the hook joke, Kyoko's caution about teasing (B0239 P20-P22), objections during the game (B0250 CL-B0250-024), the apology to Honoka (B0251 508021704), and an unchecked inference that turns care into intrusive control and survives disclosure (B0255 CL-B0255-016, EV-B0255-043, -044). Not C: they remain located occasions, not a model of when the limits apply. Not E: they recur across six readings.

Only relative markers: next week, pre-debut, a summer reference (B0250), after the live (B0251 200500), Christmas (B0251 200510), and a summer title with 'the day after tomorrow' for a two-night trip (B0255 chapter 1). No year, age or placement relative to Main is given by any reading.

scenario_readiness.note: Her Japanese is mostly paraphrased. The located wording is a message title, an address, くすぐったい and B0255's premise-bound comic spellings, and every voice cue is unheard. B0248 and B0255 give multi-speaker structure but little quoted ordinary speech. Generated lines would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Rena's speech.

The effort-and-pleasure and care-with-unchecked-inference patterns are located in unordered occurrences with mostly paraphrased speech and uncurated main-story states. Extending them to a new situation would require inventing chronology, voice and counterparts' answers.

scenario_readiness.note: Running, shopping, a museum visit, drinks, tea, party planning and beach volleyball answer bounded canon questions about these occurrences. Most outings and purchases are proposed or reported, and the readings give no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation.

Apologies after teasing, recognition of staff labor and a situated decision to disclose despite possible trouble for the manager (B0248 505018303; B0251 508021701, 508021704; B0255 EV-B0255-037) are the only normative content. They cannot support simulating ethical deliberation in another situation.

The readings affirmatively deny an established romance: D's 'near my type, for now enough', G's qualified date comparison and the contested 'courting an idol' exchange (B0199 H:P274-P275) keep both positions; B0239 and B0248 claim no reciprocal romance; B0255 completes Kyoko's romantic reading of Rena's 'yes' privately as worry about the wig (EV-B0255-027). Simulating a romance would invent a relationship the evidence withholds.

Idol work appears in breadth (making-of filming, recording nerves, joint practice, post-live planning, a PV shoot), but every performance is reported or elided and appraisals belong to peers, staff or the director (B0248; B0250 EV-B0250-024; B0251 200500; B0255 EV-B0255-029, -039). CONDITIONAL would need a procedure the readings do not supply.

known_limits.statement: The sources are independent conditional occurrences with no total chronology, year or unlock level; only B0199 H and each Event family have an internal order, and cross-case comparisons are thematic.

No performance outcome is shown: the higher-bar attempt has no result (B0199 H5), the making-of footage is not supplied (B0248), the dance contest is elided with no winner (B0250), the 2nd GEAR concert and the Christmas event are reported (B0251), and the PV shoot's recovery is staff appraisal and Coney's report (B0255).
No reciprocal romance is established; her appraisals of the manager are qualified, the courting exchange is contested, and in B0255 her ambiguous 'yes' is privately completed as worry about the wig.

Her teasing and body jokes draw explicit objections and at least two apologies, the manager's unannounced touch draws her protest, and her unrequested protection stops a colleague's care and a consultation; candid play or care is not standing consent for any party.

In B0255 her hairpiece belief is never checked, survives the well disclosure and reaches the manager as a baldness assurance at the ending; the reading keeps it as her inference, not a fact about him.

The recovery in B0199 is a local turning point: she asks for a higher bar at once and the coda reports a complaint about nonstop dancing; later readings state that her current competence does not cure earlier dual-success demands.
The earlier main-story and Sub readings the readings cite (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, so her main-story states are not assessed.
No performed voice, music or runtime was reviewed by any reading, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.

dimensions.note: Episode 401006487 gives a located conflict: Rena (荒木レナ) conceals strain while comparing herself with specialists in high jump and dance (P177-183), recovers a remembered pleasure in jumping after a low bar (P205-216), chooses both activities because she likes them (P226-231) and at once asks for a bar above her personal best (P245). The reading rejects both a no-change and a triumph-only reading. It is one portfolio and one relationship; no conditional rule extends it, so C is not supported.

Only episode 401006487 has an internal order; the seven short addresses are routes with no chronology, and the reading forbids harmonizing them (for example, the shoe-selection accounts in 401001210 and 401006487). Earlier states are not enrolled. Change within one episode only.

The reading paraphrases speech acts rather than quoting Rena's Japanese: a tentative question about closeness, teasing paired with admitted nervousness, explicit withdrawal of a joke, the qualified near-my-type, the not-a-child protest and requested support. Register, self-reference and address forms are not in evidence, and the 33 voice references were not heard.

Several ordinary activities are located: offering a towel and a partly used sports drink, wanting help to buy cute running shoes, a proposed morning run, an animal film she usually watched alone and a proposed meal, the pet fantasy, running on a day off and choosing shoes after one tears. A good spread within one portfolio; purchases, meals and routines remain proposed rather than shown.

The evidence is almost entirely Rena with the manager: requested closeness, criteria for being seen as herself, protests against being carried, treated as a child and touched without warning, and a requested slap on the back. The shopkeeper is occurrence-local, and Kyoko and Honoka appear only as her attribution. One relation does not support recipient conditioning.

Parenthesized inward lines are kept distinct from speech (P251-252: the limit she could not pass, no longer picturing failure), and her remembered first pleasure is her present narration. Local and brief.

Bounded disagreements: the request to be put down and that a shoulder would have sufficed (P92-95), the startled objection to the foot grasp and to being touched in public (P157-160), suspicion of the shopkeeper, the negotiated one higher attempt and the contested courting exchange (P274-275). No sustained interpersonal conflict.
No ethical deliberation by Rena is analyzed. The consent questions in the shop concern the manager's conduct; nothing is established about her ethical reasoning.

Teasing is located across several addresses: the playful refusal to let him go, the used-drink tease with admitted nervousness, the withdrawn pet joke, the qualified date comparison, the guess-who arrival and playful reprisal in the shop. A short repertoire, not a model of when she plays.

The family is complete: eight occurrences with exact scripts and hashes, all 277 Japanese and name records, every native object, sprite output and background reported as read or viewed, with 81 context rows compared. It is still one portfolio; earlier readings are not enrolled and no performed audio or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative limits are located: dance is hard despite athletic training (401000135), concealed overwork inferred from two-week shoe wear and wounds (P140-161), a plateau in high jump and dance errors (P177), the immediate return of competitive ambition, and the coda's complaint that she will dance forever. The higher-bar result is not shown and must not be filled from the separate personal-best report.

The reading affirmatively establishes that no chronology, calendar or unlock level orders the occurrences, and no Main arc date is assigned to the unnamed earlier incident. Only within-episode order is fixed.

known_limits.statement: The eight sources are conditional occurrences with no chronology or unlock level; only episode 401006487 has an internal sequence, and cross-case comparisons are thematic.
The higher-bar attempt has no shown result, and the healed foot and improved performance are Rena's self-reports without examination or measurement.

The manager's unannounced foot grasp produced useful information but drew her objection; the reading does not treat the means as consensual, and her later requested slap on the back is a different kind of support.
No performed voice, singing, music, sound or continuous runtime was heard or watched, and the promised live is not performed in the source.
Her choice of both activities is a local turning point; the reading says it establishes no permanent cure for overwork, and the coda's complaint keeps the problem of limits open.

The earlier Rena readings (B0085, B0122, B0123, B0159, B0161, B0167, B0186, B0191) are not curated on this subject, so the reading's comparisons with them were not checked. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
